ENVR 101.description: Analysis of environmental issues and the role of science in their identification and resolution.
ENVR 101.subject: ENVR
ENVR 101.title: Introduction to the Environment

ENVR 101L.description: Demonstrations, field trips, data analyses, and discussion relating to environmental issues, such as sustainability, resource management, and pollution control.
ENVR 101L.subject: ENVR
ENVR 101L.title: Introduction to the Environment Lab

ENVR 121.description: Interdisciplinary seminar combining the intellectual exploration of ecological perspectives with the physical exploration of the local environment. First-year students only.
ENVR 121.subject: ENVR
ENVR 121.title: Green Explorations

ENVR 122.description: Interdisciplinary seminar on designing, researching, and implementing collaborative projects to promote ecological sustainability. First-year students only.
ENVR 122.subject: ENVR
ENVR 122.title: Green Engagements

ENVR 200.description: General review of plants, animals, and geological features of South Carolina, with an emphasis on connections to the natural world.
ENVR 200.subject: ENVR
ENVR 200.title: Natural History of South Carolina

ENVR 201.description: Introduction to interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspectives on environmental issues. Required for majors in the Environment and Sustainability Program. Integrative case studies address ways of understanding nature. Sophomore Standing.
ENVR 201.subject: ENVR
ENVR 201.title: Environmental Science and Policy I

ENVR 202.description: Continuing interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary exploration of relations between environment and society for majors in the Environment and Sustainability Program. Case studies raise issues, challenges, and strategies to achieving sustainability.
ENVR 202.subject: ENVR
ENVR 202.title: Environmental Science and Policy II

ENVR 231.description: Introduction to development, establishment, and implementation of sustainability management systems and organizational leadership for achieving environmental, social, and economic goals.
ENVR 231.subject: ENVR
ENVR 231.title: Introduction to Sustainability Management and Leadership

ENVR 295.description: Examination of roots and culture of environmentalism and related technological innovation in Germany. Comparison of green practices around the world to practices within Europe and U.S.
ENVR 295.subject: ENVR
ENVR 295.title: Green Technology in Germany

ENVR 310.description: Environmental considerations of the hydrologic cycle. Occurrence and movement of surface water and groundwater as they relate to water budgets, water supply, and ecosystems. Geochemistry of natural waters, water quality, and pollution.
ENVR 310.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in MATH 122 or MATH 141; C or higher in GEOL 101, GEOL 103, GEOL 201, GEOG 104, GEOG 201, ENVR 101, ENVR 201, ECIV 101 or MSCI 101.
ENVR 310.subject: ENVR
ENVR 310.title: Surface and Subsurface Hydrology

ENVR 316.description: An exploration of the science behind oil spills, toxic chemicals, microplastics, and other organic pollutants impacting our oceans, from coastlines to the deep-sea. Emphasis on how these contaminants move, transform, and affect marine life and human health, and how cutting-edge science drives legal action and policy change.
ENVR 316.subject: ENVR
ENVR 316.title: Marine Organic Pollution

ENVR 321.description: A survey of pollution (chemical, biological, physical) effects on environmental quality and public health with emphases on how each pollutant class behaves and affects individual and community health over acute to chronic exposure periods.
ENVR 321.subject: ENVR
ENVR 321.title: Environmental Pollution and Health

ENVR 322.description: Examination of principles and arguments surrounding moral issues involving the environment.
ENVR 322.subject: ENVR
ENVR 322.title: Environmental Ethics

ENVR 323.description: Concerns in global environmental health, with a focus on toxic pollution and disease burden in developing countries. Investigation of international treaties, corresponding environmental pollution processes, and human health effects.
ENVR 323.subject: ENVR
ENVR 323.title: Global Environmental Health

ENVR 331.description: Multidisciplinary approach to interrelated environmental, economic and social problems facing humans at local, regional and global scales.
ENVR 331.subject: ENVR
ENVR 331.title: Integrating Sustainability

ENVR 342.subject: ENVR
ENVR 342.title: Environmental Anthropology: Cross-cultural Perspectives on Environmental Change

ENVR 348.description: History of the environmental justice movement and the unequal distribution of environmental harms on low income, minority, and historically marginalized groups.
ENVR 348.subject: ENVR
ENVR 348.title: Environmental Racism and Justice

ENVR 352.description: The role of energy in shaping society and geographic settings, as well as how energy production and consumption are shaped by the societal values and norms in which it is extracted, produced, and consumed.
ENVR 352.subject: ENVR
ENVR 352.title: Energy, Society and Sustainability

ENVR 360.description: Exploration of post-graduation opportunities in academia and industry. Interactive discussion of topics including helping skills, active listening, oral communication, goal setting, interviewing, and building a strong professional portfolio.
ENVR 360.subject: ENVR
ENVR 360.title: SEOE Peer Mentorship, Leadership, Professional Development

ENVR 365.description: Computational analysis of earth, marine, and environmental datasets applying time series analysis, regression, filtering, and statistical analysis.
ENVR 365.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 106 or higher; C or better in MATH 122 or higher.
ENVR 365.subject: ENVR
ENVR 365.title: Data Science in Earth, Ocean and Environmental Science

ENVR 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and dean of the School of the Environment is required for undergraduate students.
ENVR 399.subject: ENVR
ENVR 399.title: Independent Study

ENVR 460.description: Field research practices and analysis techniques in environmental science. Combines inquiry-based field investigations at Congaree National Park and laboratory sample analysis with integration of data and public policy concepts. Daily field trips required.
ENVR 460.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ENVR 201 and ENVR 202.
ENVR 460.subject: ENVR
ENVR 460.title: Congaree National Park: Field Investigations in Environmental Science

ENVR 480.description: Collaborative study of a contemporary environmental issue. Field trips may be required.
ENVR 480.subject: ENVR
ENVR 480.title: Capstone Seminar in Environmental Science and Environmental Studies

ENVR 490.description: Current developments in sustainability and global environmental issues selected to meet faculty and student interests. May be repeated as content varies.
ENVR 490.subject: ENVR
ENVR 490.title: Special Topics in Sustainability and the Environment

ENVR 495.description: Supervised internship experience in a professional environment within the field of the environment and/or related environmental sciences or studies. Undergraduate internship contract required with approval of instructor, advisor, and department head before registration.
ENVR 495.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ENVR 201 and ENVR 202.
ENVR 495.subject: ENVR
ENVR 495.title: Internship in the Environment

ENVR 499.description: Independent student research in collaboration with faculty mentors. Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required.
ENVR 499.subject: ENVR
ENVR 499.title: Research in Environmental Science

ENVR 500.description: Multidisciplinary research projects related to University or community environmental problems (e.g., energy, water conservation, solid waste, recycling).
ENVR 500.subject: ENVR
ENVR 500.title: Environmental Practicum

ENVR 501.description: An in-depth analysis course of a specific interdisciplinary environmental topic. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
ENVR 501.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ENVR 101 or ENVR 201 or graduate standing.
ENVR 501.subject: ENVR
ENVR 501.title: Special Topics in the Environment

ENVR 503.description: An overview of the microbial world including a survey of the distribution, functioning, and diversity of microorganisms in natural systems. Discusses the crucial roles that microorganisms play in ecosystem function, biogeochemical cycles, and environmental quality.
ENVR 503.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MSCI 102 or BIOL 102; C or better in CHEM 112.
ENVR 503.subject: ENVR
ENVR 503.title: Environmental Microbiology

ENVR 504.description: This course will discuss the urgent need for deploying solar radiation and carbon dioxide removal approaches at scale, including potential benefits and risks of these options. It will also discuss regulatory and governance considerations at both the national and international level and strategizes to incentivize large-scale adoption of these approaches.
ENVR 504.subject: ENVR
ENVR 504.title: Climate Geoengineering

ENVR 506.description: Application of the principles of ecology with the methods of engineering to design sustainable ecosystems to better integrate human society with the coastal environment.
ENVR 506.subject: ENVR
ENVR 506.title: Coastal Nature-Based Solutions

ENVR 517.description: A discussion-based seminar course that examines nature-society relations in coastal regions globally. The course will use social theory to understand how uneven development processes shaped – and continue shaping – current coastlines. We will explore key topics including coastal capitalism, delta ecologies, and climate justice via several global case studies.
ENVR 517.subject: ENVR
ENVR 517.title: Socionatural Coastlines in Global Perspective

ENVR 531.description: Integrated management system principles and advanced leadership strategies to create sustainable development initiatives.
ENVR 531.subject: ENVR
ENVR 531.title: Sustainability Management and Leadership Strategies

ENVR 533.description: Research, development and implementation of sustainability projects throughout the campus and community.
ENVR 533.subject: ENVR
ENVR 533.title: Sustainability Projects Course

ENVR 534.description: Interdisciplinary examination of the global policy challenge of ensuring equitable access to water and sanitation services for all.
ENVR 534.subject: ENVR
ENVR 534.title: Water and Sanitation in Global Perspective

ENVR 538.description: Political, social, and cultural landscapes of food and farming around the world; issues of agricultural production, trade, consumption, and food security.
ENVR 538.subject: ENVR
ENVR 538.title: Global Food Politics

ENVR 540.description: Critical examination of the ways ideas about nature and racial difference are conceptually and materially entwined with the production of social and environmental inequalities.
ENVR 540.subject: ENVR
ENVR 540.title: Decolonizing the Environment: Race, Nature, Power

ENVR 548.description: An analysis of the economics aspects of environmental decay, pollution control, and natural resource use. Analysis of the ability of the market system to allocate resources efficiently when economic activity is accompanied by environmental damage. Discussion of alternative public policy approaches to pollution control and natural resource conservation.
ENVR 548.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECON 221 and ECON 222 or C or better in ECON 224.
ENVR 548.subject: ENVR
ENVR 548.title: Environmental Economics

ENVR 571.description: Principles of conservation biology. Importance of biodiversity, causes of decline and extinction, and restoration and conversation policy in terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.
ENVR 571.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301.
ENVR 571.subject: ENVR
ENVR 571.title: Conservation Biology

ENVR 572.description: Quantitative study of the population, community and evolutionary ecology of freshwater habitats (lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, wetlands). Includes mandatory fieldtrips.
ENVR 572.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301.
ENVR 572.subject: ENVR
ENVR 572.title: Freshwater Ecology

ENVR 700.description: Current issues, policies, and regulations pertaining to environmental studies. Emphasizes integrated multidisciplinary approaches toward identification, evaluation, preservation, mitigation, and/or utilization of environmentally sensitive material and sites.
ENVR 700.subject: ENVR
ENVR 700.title: Current Topics in Environmental Studies

ENVR 706.description: Application of the principles of ecology with the methods of engineering to design sustainable ecosystems to better integrate human society with the coastal environment.
ENVR 706.subject: ENVR
ENVR 706.title: Coastal Nature-Based Solutions

ENVR 709.description: This course provides a hands-on, project-oriented investigation of current approaches for research in marine science, ecology and environmental science. Components of the course will include exploratory data analyses, statistics, graphics and the R programming language. Prior programming experience is beneficial, but not required.
ENVR 709.subject: ENVR
ENVR 709.title: Marine Data Science with R

ENVR 725.description: International environmental management systems standards will be integrated with business planning to provide students with the best strategies for future growth in today’s environmentally sensitive global economy.
ENVR 725.subject: ENVR
ENVR 725.title: International Environmental Management Systems

ENVR 790.description: Directed research topics to be individually assigned.
ENVR 790.subject: ENVR
ENVR 790.title: Directed Individual Studies

ENVR 795.description: Preparation and presentation of a capstone project plan for conduct of multidisciplinary environmental research addressing public/private/non-profit sector issues through an internship in government agencies, NGOs or private industry.
ENVR 795.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: One semester full-time graduate enrollment or equivalent.
ENVR 795.subject: ENVR
ENVR 795.title: Environmental Internship Preparation

ENVR 796.description: Environmental internship in government agencies, NGOs, or private industry, culminating in a project deliverable. Typically includes data analyses/metrics, resource management options, and/or internal outreach education, with final assessment. Restricted to graduate students in the MEERM program.
ENVR 796.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: 3 credits of ENVR 795; successful completion of MEERM comprehensive examination.
ENVR 796.subject: ENVR
ENVR 796.title: Environmental Internship

ENVR 800.description: Examination of the effectiveness of environmental policies and methods relative to current issues and needs.
ENVR 800.subject: ENVR
ENVR 800.title: Seminar in Environmental Studies

ENVR 802.description: An examination of issues related to environmental policy making, implementation and management.
ENVR 802.subject: ENVR
ENVR 802.title: Environmental Policy and Management

ENVR 804.description: This seminar is designed to explore and develop practical advocacy skills in the area of environmental representation and to provide an understanding of advocacy in administrative, legislative, and litigation arenas.
ENVR 804.subject: ENVR
ENVR 804.title: Environmental Advocacy Seminar

ENVR 835.description: Examination of the intellectual, cultural, and ethical frameworks within which environmental problems arise and are solved.
ENVR 835.subject: ENVR
ENVR 835.title: Seminar in Environmental Ethics
